summary: Everyone except citizens of India, Bangladesh and the Maldives needs a Bhutan visa, applied for online (US$40) directly or through a licensed tour operator, and every visitor pays the Sustainable Development Fee — US$100 per person per night for most foreigners. Indian nationals instead obtain an entry permit and pay a lower daily fee.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in Bhutan. Indian nationals may alternatively use a voter identity card at the land border.

source.name: Department of Immigration, Bhutan — official visa and permit portal

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required only if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

source.name: Department of Immigration, Bhutan — official visa and permit portal

travelInsurance.text: Valid travel insurance covering the full duration of your stay is required for the tourist visa — proof is requested during the online application.

source.name: Department of Immigration, Bhutan — official visa and permit portal

onwardTicket.text: No separate onward-ticket check — flights into Paro are limited to Drukair and Bhutan Airlines, so confirmed bookings are effectively part of every itinerary.

source.name: Department of Immigration, Bhutan — official visa and permit portal

proofOfFunds.text: Not required. The visa fee and Sustainable Development Fee are paid before the visa is issued.

source.name: Department of Immigration, Bhutan — official visa and permit portal

currencyLimits.text: Foreign currency worth more than US$10,000 (or equivalent) must be declared on arrival.

source.name: Department of Immigration, Bhutan — official visa and permit portal

notes: Tobacco may be imported only in small quantities for personal use and attracts high duties; smoking is banned in most public places.
Antiques and religious artefacts may not be exported. Buy handicrafts from licensed shops and keep the receipts for customs.

payments.text: Cards are accepted at better hotels and handicraft shops in Thimphu and Paro, but Bhutan is largely cash-based. The ngultrum is pegged 1:1 to the Indian rupee, and rupees are widely accepted.

safety.text: Bhutan is one of Asia's safest destinations, with very low crime. The practical risks are altitude on treks, winding mountain roads and stray dogs — not people.

bestTimeToVisit.text: Spring (March–May) brings rhododendron blooms and mild trekking weather; fall (September–November) offers the clearest Himalayan views and the biggest tsechu festivals.

tips.text: Budget for the Sustainable Development Fee before anything else: US$100 per person per night for most visitors (US$50 for children 6–12, free under 6), paid upfront when the visa is issued. Indian nationals pay ₹1,200 per night instead.

Only Drukair and Bhutan Airlines fly into Paro — one of the world's most demanding airports, where flights are weather-dependent and sell out around festival season. Book flights before anything else and keep a buffer day for connections.

Since the 2023 reforms you can explore Thimphu and Paro independently, but a licensed guide is still required for treks and travel beyond the main western valleys. The rules are refined periodically, so check when applying. Most visitors simply book through a licensed Bhutanese operator.
Passes on popular routes climb well above 3,000 m and treks go much higher — build in acclimatisation days, and take even the day hike to Tiger's Nest (3,120 m) slowly.
To enter dzongs and temples, wear long sleeves and long trousers or a skirt, remove shoes and hats, and photograph only where permitted — never inside shrine rooms.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Bhutan?
faq.answer: Yes, unless you hold an Indian, Bangladeshi or Maldivian passport. Everyone else applies online at visit.doi.gov.bt — directly or through a licensed tour operator — paying a US$40 visa fee plus the Sustainable Development Fee, and the visa is issued for your exact travel dates before arrival.

faq.question: How much is Bhutan's Sustainable Development Fee?
faq.answer: US$100 per person per night for most foreign visitors, with discounts for children (US$50 for ages 6–12, free under 6). Indian nationals pay ₹1,200 per night. The fee funds healthcare, education and conservation, and is paid before your visa or permit is issued.

faq.question: Do Indian citizens need a visa for Bhutan?
faq.answer: No visa, but they need an entry permit — obtainable online at visit.doi.gov.bt or on arrival at Paro airport and the Phuentsholing land border, using a passport or voter identity card, and they pay the ₹1,200-per-night Sustainable Development Fee.

faq.question: Do I have to book a tour to visit Bhutan?
faq.answer: No — since the 2022–2023 reforms, independent visits are allowed and you can apply for the visa yourself. A licensed guide is still required for treks and for travel beyond the main western valleys, so many visitors find a licensed Bhutanese operator the simplest route.

faq.question: How do I apply for a Bhutan visa?
faq.answer: Apply online at visit.doi.gov.bt with your passport, a photo, proof of travel insurance for the full stay, and payment of the US$40 visa fee plus the Sustainable Development Fee. Processing typically takes around 5 business days, and the visa clearance is checked at check-in for your Paro flight.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Bhutan?
faq.answer: Yes — extensions are possible through the Department of Immigration portal or your operator, provided you pay the Sustainable Development Fee for the additional nights. Arrange it before your current visa period ends.
